summary: The recorded base reproduces the Inkling first-block tool-header leak in one-shot and streamed parsing. The exact candidate removes the visible tool name while retaining the correctly parsed tool call for both modes. Its focused regression suite and independent JSON/raw-text, empty-header, chunk-boundary, ordinary-text, and continue_final_message cases pass.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual InklingDetector then FunctionCallParser behavior: missing-opener input leaked visible 'get_weather' in both one-shot and 7-character streamed modes while still producing get_weather({}).
The same parser-chain reproduction produced empty visible content and the correct tool call for missing-opener, explicit-opener, and thinking-first inputs in one-shot and streamed modes.
367 tests and 68 subtests passed on the exact candidate, covering the changed reasoning parser and downstream function-call parser.

Five independent one-shot cases and fifteen streamed chunking cases passed, including JSON and raw-text tools, empty headers, ordinary text, text preceding a model block, plus immediate continue_final_message output.

gpu_execution.evidence: The original issue and candidate change are deterministic Python parser logic and require neither model execution nor GPU kernels; no GPU claim is made.

remaining_limitations: No full HTTP server or real Inkling model/weights were exercised; this review validates the parser chain that the issue identifies, not model semantic quality or serving infrastructure.
No native rebuild was applicable because the candidate changes only Python parser code and tests.

A streamed input ending in an incomplete control-token prefix drops that suffix on finish, but a direct base comparison showed the same pre-existing behavior; it is outside the reported complete tool-invocation contract and is not introduced by the candidate.
